273:
(a) All alcoholic beverage licenses shall henceforth be classified as follows:
(1) Class I license means that license granted to any person by Georgetown-Quitman County to an applicant for the sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages sold at wholesale to any valid alcoholic beverage licensee.
(2) Class II license means that license granted to any persons by Georgetown-Quitman County to an applicant for package sales of wine and malt beverages sold at retail to the public for consumption off the premises.
(3) Class III license means that license granted to any persons by Georgetown-Quitman County to an applicant for package sales of distilled spirits sold at retail to the public for consumption off the premises.
(4) Class IV license means that license granted to any person by Georgetown-Quitman County to an applicant for an on-premises beer and wine consumption license at a location that meets the definition of a restaurant under this chapter.
(5) Class V license means that license granted to any person by Georgetown-Quitman County to an applicant for an on-premises distilled spirits consumption license at a location that meets the definition of a restaurant under this chapter.
(b) All applications and licenses issued hereafter shall be in keeping with the above classifications.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
274:
A separate alcoholic beverage license is hereby required for each place of business when such application includes various classes of licenses (Class I, II, III, IV, V).
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
275:
Georgetown-Quitman County shall endeavor to accumulate and maintain a complete file of licenses granted under the terms and conditions of this chapter. Such file may contain any information deemed appropriate by the Georgetown-Quitman County, and may include applications, investigative reports, licenses issued, incidents involving licensee and/or place of business, code and/or building violations, hearings/results, premises inspections, photographs and other such information and data that may assist Georgetown-Quitman County in the determination of the decision to grant, renew, transfer, name change or other license actions required and/or applied for within Georgetown-Quitman County.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
278:
No pending or future application for a Georgetown-Quitman County alcoholic beverage license shall be approved by Georgetown-Quitman County unless it appears that all material and valid requirements of this chapter have been met by the applicant and that the applicant is qualified to hold a license, should it be issued, under this chapter. In addition, all applicants for a Georgetown-Quitman County alcoholic beverage license in the county must have all local taxes paid in full at the time said application is submitted, (with the exception of any taxes which are in arbitration) and must have first paid the county all money, taxes or otherwise, due and owed as of the date the application is submitted.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Ord. No. O2-2020, 3-9-20)
279:
No new alcoholic beverage license shall be issued until first having received approval of the license application by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
280:
All applicants for an alcoholic beverage license shall comply with the following application procedure:
(1) All applications for an alcoholic beverage license shall be submitted on forms provided for that purpose by Georgetown-Quitman County Clerk and shall be approved by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County prior to the issuance of the license applied for.
(2) The application shall include but shall not be limited to: the name and address of the applicant; the proposed business to be carried on; if a partnership, the names and residence address of the partners; if a limited liability company, L.L.C., the name and address of the manager(s) and the name of any person or legal entity owning any percentage of the L.L.C.; if a corporation, the names of the officers, the name and address of the registered agent for service of process, the name of the officer(s), and the name of all shareholders of any class of corporate stock, or any other entity having a financial interest in each entity which is to own or operate the establishment for which a license is sought. If the manager changes, the applicant must furnish the commission the name and address of the new manager and other information as requested within ten days of such change.
(3) All applicants shall furnish data, fingerprints, financial responsibility and other records as required by the licensing and revenue manager and to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article. Failure to furnish data, pursuant to such request shall automatically serve to dismiss the application with prejudice.
(4) All applications shall be sworn to by the applicant before a notary public or other officer empowered by law to administer oaths as to the information contained in the application and to any other information required or contained within the application and accompanying information and by this chapter.
(5) In all instances in which an application is denied under the provisions of this chapter the applicant may not reapply for a license for at least one year from the final date of such denial.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
281:
Any applicant for an alcoholic beverage license shall meet the minimum qualifications upon the submission of an application for same, as follows:
(1) Be 21 years of age, or older.
(2) Meet all minimum requirements for such license imposed by the state.
(3) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person who is not a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
(4) Where the applicant is a partnership, limited liability company or corporation, the provisions of this section shall apply to all its partners, officers, manager(s) and stockholders. In the case of a corporation the license shall be issued jointly to the corporation and a stockholder, if an individual. Where the majority stockholder is not an individual, the license shall be issued jointly to the corporation and its agent registered under the provisions of this chapter. In the case of a partnership the license will be issued to all the partners. In the case of a limited liability company, the license will be issued jointly to the limited liability company and manager(s).
(5) The license applicant and all employees thereof shall not have been convicted within ten years of the date of application of any felony, misdemeanor, excepting minor traffic violations, or any violations of the laws or ordinances of Georgetown-Quitman County, state or United States relating to the distribution, sale or dispensing of alcoholic beverages or any crime involving moral turpitude. A plea of nolo contendere for any felony or misdemeanor of any city, state or federal court, or a forfeiture of a bond when charged with a crime is hereby considered a conviction under this chapter; provided, however, where the violation is for a misdemeanor or the forfeiture of bond involves a municipal ordinance, Georgetown-Quitman County in its discretion may waive such disqualification.
(6) No person, firm limited liability company or corporation shall be granted any alcoholic beverage license unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the commission, or its designee, that such person, manager(s), partners in the firm, or officers and directors of the corporation have not been convicted or plead guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to, and have been released from parole or probation concerning any crime involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling or illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or the illegal possession or sale of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in a manner contrary to law, keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexual related crime within a period of ten years immediately prior to the filing of such application. At the time an application is submitted for any alcoholic beverage license, the applicant shall, by a duly sworn affidavit, certify that neither the applicant, nor any of the other owners of the establishment has been convicted or has pleaded guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any crime involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling or illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or the illegal possession or sale of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in a manner contrary to law, keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexual-related crime within a period of ten years immediately prior to the filing of such application. Should any applicant, partner, or officer instrumental in the sale or dispensing of any alcoholic beverage, after a license has been granted, be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling or illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or the illegal possession or sale of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in a manner contrary to law, keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexual-related crime, the license shall be immediately revoked and cancelled.
(7) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person convicted under any federal, state or local law of any felony, within ten years prior to the filing of application for such license.
(8) It shall be unlawful for any county employee directly involved in the issuance of alcoholic beverage licenses under this chapter, to have any whole, partial or beneficial interest in any license to sell alcoholic beverages in the county.
(9) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person who has had any license issued under the police powers of the county previously revoked within two years prior to the filing of the application.
(10) The commission may decline to issue a license when any person having any ownership interest in the operation of such place of business or control over such place of business does not meet the same character requirements as herein set forth for the licensee.
(11) All licensed establishments must have and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter to be served upon the licensee or owner may be served. This person must be a resident of Georgetown-Quitman County. The licensee shall file the name of such agent, along with the written consent of such agent with the commission and shall be in such form as may be prescribed by the commission.
(12) All applicants for any alcoholic beverage license must be of good character, and all operators, managers, clerks, or other employees shall be of like character. Corporate or firm applicants shall be of good business reputation.
(13) A license application may be denied to any applicant for any alcoholic beverage license where it appears that the applicant would not have adequate financial participation in the proposed business to direct and manage its affairs, or where it appears that the application is intended to be a mere surrogate for a person or persons who would not otherwise qualify for a license for any reason whatsoever.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Ord. No. O3-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 9-12-23)
282:
The applicant shall make a sworn statement of his qualifications according to the terms and conditions of this chapter, and shall file same with the manager of Georgetown-Quitman County prior to any approval of application or license issuance.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
283:
Any misstatement or concealment of fact by the applicant shall be grounds for revocation of license issued and shall make the applicant liable to prosecution for perjury under the laws or ordinances of Georgetown-Quitman County, state and/or United States Government.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
285:
If the applicant/licensee for an alcoholic beverage license shall assign, allow, direct or permit the management, operations or conduct of the alcoholic beverage business by a party or parties other than himself, the party and/or parties managing, directing, conducting or operating such business shall be deemed equally responsible and subject to all conditions of this chapter in every respect in the same manner and degree as the owner.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
286:
(a) The manager, operator or designee shall be that person designated by the licensee as responsible for the management and/or conduct of business connected with the operation of a licensed alcoholic beverage establishment, Class I, Class II, Class III, Class IV or Class V. The manager, operator or designee shall devote and be on the premises of the licensee a minimum of 30 hours per work week and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of this chapter.
(b) It shall be the responsibility of the alcoholic beverage licensee to notify the Georgetown-Quitman County Manager within 48 hours in writing of any change made by the licensee in the manager, operator or designee for the operation of the licensed premises.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
287:
Georgetown-Quitman County shall have the right to accept or reject such manager, operator and/or designee based upon the results of an investigation of the record of the individual. The licensee shall be notified, in writing, by the Georgetown-Quitman County Manager as to the results of such investigation within 72 hours of such determination.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
288:
All applicants for an alcoholic beverage license within Georgetown-Quitman County shall be fingerprinted in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2 which same shall be submitted to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation in accordance with said law, who in turn shall submit same to the FBI and a record shall be returned to Georgetown-Quitman County as provided for by said statute. Georgetown-Quitman County shall have the right to issue or reject such application based solely upon the results of the investigation. No license shall be issued without said report.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
289:
The applicant shall furnish such other information as the Georgetown-Quitman County Manager may, upon direction of the commission, from time to time require.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
290:
The applicant shall sign an agreement that, in consideration of the privilege of approval of the application/license, the applicant shall pay all taxes, fees, levies, etc., imposed upon the licensee by this chapter and will sell or hold for sale no alcoholic beverage upon which such taxes, fees, levies, etc., have not been paid.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
291:
All applicants for a new alcoholic beverage license within Georgetown-Quitman County shall be required to have a public hearing conducted by the commission prior to the issuance of such license.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
292:
(a) For existing consumption off-premises and/or on-premises licensed establishments. A special event alcohol permit may be issued to any establishment licensed to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on-premises to allow such establishment to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption within the fixed boundaries of the physical area where a special event is proposed to be held. The licensee must submit an application and pay the required non-refundable fee(s), and, in relation to the special event alcohol permit, shall be required to comply with all licensing requirements associated with its consumption on-premises license. Notwithstanding any other term or prohibition in this chapter, the holder of the special event alcohol permit may be authorized, upon terms and conditions identified by the county manager, to pour alcohol at the special event and allow open container consumption within the fixed boundaries of the physical area where the special event is to be held. An establishment that holds a current on-premises consumption license may not receive a special event alcohol permit for package sales for off-premises consumption.
(b) For non-profit civic organizations. A special event alcohol permit may be issued to a non-profit charitable civic organization. The applicant must submit an application and pay any required non-refundable fee(s) and shall be required to comply with all licensing requirements for a consumption on-premises establishment. Notwithstanding any other term or prohibition in this chapter, the holder of a special event alcohol permit may be authorized, upon terms and conditions identified by the county manager, to pour alcohol at the special event, sell sealed packaged beer and/or wine for off-premises consumption, and allow open container consumption within the fixed boundaries of the physical area where the special event is to be held. In the event that open container consumption is so authorized within the fixed boundaries of the physical area where the special event is to be held, any other holder of a consumption on-premises license whose licensed premises is located entirely within the fixed boundary of the special event site shall likewise be authorized to allow open container alcohol consumption within the special event boundary. This open container consumption accommodation shall only be authorized, if at all, during the term of the special event.
(c) Submission of application. All applications must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the proposed date of the special event.
(d) Permit not required. Any employee or volunteer of a non-profit charitable civic organization special event alcohol permit, working the special event in any position dispensing, selling, serving, taking orders or mixing alcoholic beverages shall not be required to obtain an alcohol seller/server permit for the special event, provided that no person under 21 years of age may dispense, serve, or take orders for alcoholic beverages.
(e) Special event criteria. The special event must be associated with and benefit the cause of a non-profit charitable civic organization.
(f) Sheriff's authority to revoke. The sheriff or his or her designee may immediately revoke any special event alcohol permit if they determine that continued alcohol sales may endanger the health, welfare, or safety of the public.
(g) Indemnification and insurance. As a condition on the issuance of a special event alcohol permit, the licensee shall indemnify and hold the Unified Government of Georgetown-Quitman County harmless from any and all claims, demands, or causes of action that may arise from activities associated with the special event. In addition, the licensee shall maintain at a minimum a $1,000,000.00 general liability insurance policy with the Unified Government of Georgetown-Quitman County and its elected officials, employees, or agents being named as additional insureds.
(Ord. No. O4-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 1-9-24)
295:
All applicants for an initial alcoholic beverage license shall, at the time of application therefore, deposit with the Manager of Georgetown-Quitman County a nonrefundable investigation fee as set by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
296:
All applicants for an initial alcohol beverage license shall deposit with the Manager of Georgetown-Quitman County a license fee for such license as set by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County. Generally, no such fees shall be prorated for any portion of a year, nor shall any such fees be refundable, unless said fees are refundable under section 6-119. Provided however, the commission may prorate fees for a portion of the year if the circumstances call for such proration as determined in the sole discretion of the commission.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
297:
(a) The annual license fee for the renewal of an alcoholic beverage license once granted shall be as set by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County.
(b) All licenses for the upcoming year must be purchased prior to December 31 of each year. Licenses expire at midnight December 31. Renewing applicants are required to be fingerprinted and pay an administration fee of $100.00 annually at renewal time.
(c) Upon application for a renewal of an alcoholic beverage license for a restaurant (Class IV and Class V licenses), a sales statement must be submitted by the license holder and the management of the establishment showing the total sales of food and alcoholic beverages and the percentage of food sales. In addition, the license holder shall submit a statement from each wholesaler from whom the licensee has purchased any type of alcohol which said statement must show the total dollar amount of alcohol beverages sold to the license holder for the license year. Georgetown-Quitman County may cause an audit of the books of a licensee to be made at any time. Each license holder, by virtue of having applied for a license, shall furnish to Georgetown-Quitman County all books and records when requested by Georgetown-Quitman County. Failure of a licensee to furnish the books and records and to cooperate in the execution of the audit shall be a violation of this chapter. An applicant shall, with the application for a Class IV and Class V licenses license, submit a projected sales statement showing the percentage of food and alcohol sales anticipated.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Amend. of 10-13-16)
298:
(a) All first time alcoholic beverage license applicants are required to be fingerprinted and pay $255.00 for the administration fee.
(b) All alcoholic beverage applicants that are renewing are required to be fingerprinted and pay an administration fee of $100.00 at renewal time.
(Ord. No. 05-2016, 10-13-16; Amend. of 10-13-16; Ord. No. O1-2019, 1-22-19)
299:
Special event alcohol permit applicants must pay the required non-refundable fee(s), as established by resolution of the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, before any permit or license will be issued hereunder.
(Ord. No. O4-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 1-9-24)
302:
All retail sales locations must meet the following minimum specifications:
(1) Must meet the building codes adopted by Georgetown-Quitman County.
(2) The interior of the building must be clearly visible from the exterior.
(3) The interior must contain lighting of such strength that the interior of the building can be clearly seen from the exterior.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
303:
No application for an alcoholic beverage license shall be approved which does not include or have attached thereto a drawing of the premises and interior and the location at which applicant desires to operate.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
304:
No alcoholic beverage license shall be granted or issued to any applicant for such license nor shall alcoholic beverages be sold, offered for sale, given or distributed from the premises of the licensee within the following distance of:
(1) Churches: within 100 yards of any church building. The term "church building" as used herein shall mean the main structure used by any religious organization for purposes of worship.
(2) Schools:
a. Distilled spirits: within 200 yards of any school building, school grounds or college campus.
b. Wine and malt beverages: within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds or college campus.
c. As used in this section, the term "school building", "school", "school grounds" or educational building" shall apply only to state, county, city, or church school buildings and to such buildings at such other schools in which are taught subjects commonly taught in the common schools, universities and colleges of this state and which are public schools or private schools as defined in O.C.G.A. § 20-2-690(b). The term "school building" and "educational building" includes only those structures in which instruction is offered. The term "school grounds" and "college campus" shall apply only to the parcel or parcels of land on which a school, school building or educational building is located. The term "college" shall mean an educational institution authorized by the state to award associate, baccalaureate or higher degrees.
(3) Libraries and/or branch libraries: within 100 yards feet of any library or branch premises thereof.
(4) Alcohol or drug treatment or counseling facility: within 100 yards.
(5) Government buildings (except as provided in section 6-21 for the central business district), public parks, recreation centers, sports or athletic facilities: within 100 yards.
(6) Any area where minors congregate: within 100 yards.
(7) Any private dwelling: within 100 feet.
(8) Class III license applications only: within 500 yards of any other business licensed to sell package liquor at retail.
(9) No location which is licensed to sell alcoholic beverages on the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter derives shall be denied continued operation under an existing license, or denied any renewal of such license, nor shall any new owner of said location be denied a new license based upon the measurements set forth in this section.
(10) As to any location licensed in the future, if the distance requirements herein are met at the time of issuance of any license, the subsequent opening and operation of a church, school, or college within the distance prohibited herein shall not prevent the continuance of an existing license or the renewal thereof or the issuance of a new license to any subsequent owner of such property.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
305:
(a) Unless otherwise provided by law, those distance measurement prohibitions stated in section 6-113 shall be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground and shall be measured in the following manner:
(1) In a straight line from the front door of the structure from which beverage alcohol is sold or offered for sale;
(2) To the front door of the building of a church, government owned treatment center or a Class III retail package store; or
(3) To the nearest property line of the real property being used for school or educational purposes.
(b) All applications shall include a drawing showing that the premises is not in violation of distances under this chapter and describing the way said distances were measured. At their sole discretion, the commission may require that the applicant furnish a survey conducted by a certified surveyor showing that the premises is in compliance with the distances under this chapter.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
State Law reference— Sales of alcoholic beverages near churches, schools or college campuses, O.C.G.A. § 3-3-21.
306:
When the license applied for under this article is for a license to be located in a building not in existence when such license application is filed or construction of such building has been commenced, but is not yet completed, a license may, if otherwise authorized hereunder, be issued for such location if the application for such license and the plans for the proposed building clearly show that such building and the distance requirements will, when completed, meet all requirements of this chapter, Georgetown-Quitman County law and the state law. The annual license fee shall not be discounted or reduced for time consumed in building operations after the license is approved, but no sales shall be made at such location until the building has been completed in accordance with the plans and conforms with all provisions of the law and this chapter.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
307:
The measurements indicated in section 6-113 as measured under section 6-114 shall not apply to any person who now holds a license if the measurement was made, at the time the license was originally issued, utilizing some other measuring method. Distance requirements shall also not apply to a Class II license where the business is a grocery store or supermarket. As used in this paragraph, the term "grocery store" or "supermarket" means a retail establishment which has at least 85 percent of its total retail floor space reserved for the sale of food and other nonalcoholic items, conducts all of its sales inside the building containing its retail floor space, where groceries and food are purchased for off the premises consumption and the total sales area of such business exceeds 15,000 square feet.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
308:
In addition to all other requirements, no Class IV and Class V licenses shall be issued to any applicant whose business does not meet the definition of a restaurant as herein defined.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
309:
(a) Applications must be filed and license fees and administration fees paid in person at the commission offices. Applications will be given priority by the date of filling, provided however, if the number of applicants is more than or equal to the number of licenses available (e.g., when two or more Class III license applications are for premises within 500 yards of another) applications filed within five business days of the initial application will proceed to approval under this chapter.
(b) A substantially incomplete or inaccurate application may not be accepted and if accepted and subsequently determined to be substantially incomplete or an inaccurate will likely make the applicant ineligible for being given priority.
(c) If there are more approved applicants than licenses available, a public drawing will be held; the time, date and place of any drawing will be posted at the commission offices and the approved applicants will be notified. The drawing will be conducted in a manner the commission deems appropriate.
(d) The license fee, will be automatically refunded to each unsuccessful drawing participant. Refund checks will be mailed within 45 days of the priority drawing. The administration fee is nonrefundable.
(e) Unsuccessful drawing participants will maintain the priority position assigned at the priority drawing. In the event a successful applicant is disqualified for a license by the State of Georgia or withdraws, the next drawing participant in order of priority will be contacted and will have 30 days to repay the previously refunded license fee, and certify that the information on the original application has not changed.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14)
312:

(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Ord. No. O3-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 9-12-23)
313:

The published notice shall include the notice of application for an initial alcoholic beverage license; time, date and place of public hearing before the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County; as well as any other information required by Georgetown-Quitman County.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Ord. No. O3-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 9-12-23)
314:

315:
Each application for an initial alcoholic beverage license on which the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County conducts a public hearing shall be granted or denied by it within a reasonable period of time from the date on which such public hearing is concluded.
(1) In determining whether or not it is in the public interest and welfare for any license applied for hereunder to be granted or denied, in addition to all the other provisions of and qualifications required by this chapter, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall be guided by the following:
a. Reputation, character. The applicant's reputation, character, trade and business associations or past business ventures, mental and physical capacity to conduct this business.
b. Previous violations of liquor laws. If the applicant is a previous holder of a license to sell alcoholic beverages whether or not he has violated any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such business.
c. Manner of conducting prior liquor business. If the applicant is a previous holder of a license to sell any type of alcohol, the manner in which he conducted the business thereunder, especially as to the necessity for unusual police observation and inspection in order to prevent the violation of any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such business.
d. Location. The location for which the license is sought, as to traffic congestion, available parking, general character of the neighborhood, pedestrian traffic, proximity to those establishments or entities listed in section 6-113 that are not within the prohibited distances set forth therein, and the feelings and attitudes of the citizens residing in the area as to the effect such an establishment would have on the adjacent and surrounding property values and on their quality of life.
e. Number of licenses in the central business district. The number of licenses already granted for similar business in the central business district, as hereinbefore defined, and the need for an additional retail outlet of alcoholic beverages in the central business district.
f. Dancing. Whether dancing will take place; whether live bands will be used; whether there will music on the inside or outside of the premises; if dancing, live bands or music is to be permitted upon the premises for which the license is sought and the applicant has previously permitted dancing upon any premises controlled or supervised by him, the manner in which he controlled and supervised such dancing to prevent any violation of any law, regulation or ordinance.
g. Previous revocation of license. If the applicant is a person whose license issued under the police powers of a governing authority which has been previously suspended or revoked or who has previously had an alcoholic beverages suspended or revoked.
h. Payment of taxes. If the applicant and business are not delinquent in the payment of any local taxes or have been chronically late in the payment of taxes or assessments.
i. Congregation of minors. Any circumstances which may cause minors to congregate at or in the vicinity of the proposed location.
j. Prior incidents. Evidence that a substantial number of incidents requiring police intervention have occurred (within two square city blocks of the proposed location, during the 24 months immediately preceding the date of application).
k. Previous denial or revocation. The denial of an initial alcoholic beverage license application or renewal thereof, or the revocation of a license, occurring within the preceding 24 months, concerning the proposed location.
(2) If the initial alcoholic beverage license application is denied, Georgetown-Quitman County shall notify the applicant in writing setting forth the reason or reasons for the denial within a reasonable period of time. The applicant may appeal the denial of the application by filing a written request with the Manager of Georgetown-Quitman County asking the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County to reconsider the application along with a filing fee of $100.00. All publication costs must also be paid in advance and no costs are refundable. The applicant shall file said request within five days of the receipt of the denial of the application. Any resident of Georgetown-Quitman County may appeal the grant of an application by filing a request for reconsideration within five days of the grant of an application along with the payment of said filing fee.
(3) If an appeal is timely filed, a notice of the filing of the request for reconsideration shall be sent to the applicant and to any other person who has requested reconsideration, and said notice shall be published in the legal organ of Quitman County for three weeks prior to the time of the hearing on reconsideration. The expense of the publication shall be paid, in advance of the hearing, by the appellant. The notice shall contain the date, time and location of the hearing. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall, at the appointed time, hear any evidence offered by the applicant and from anyone opposing the issuance of the license. The applicant and appellant may be represented by counsel, may offer testimony by witnesses or any other evidence and may question any opposing witnesses. Formal evidentiary rules shall not apply and the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County may hear and consider any evidence which would be helpful to them in making a decision. At the close of the evidence, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall either deny or approve the issuance of a license.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Ord. No. O3-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 9-12-23)
316:
Applications for the renewal of alcoholic beverage licenses shall not require a public hearing thereon unless written objections thereto are filed in writing with the Manager of Georgetown-Quitman County a minimum of 15 working days prior to such renewal. A hearing of such objection shall be conducted by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County after publication of notice thereof as set forth in section 6-172.
(Ord. No. 02-14, 10-14-14; Ord. No. O3-2023, § 1(Exh. A), 9-12-23)
